name: Default First-Time Setup — orkes login to Developer Edition
expected_behavior: Step 1: Treat an unqualified first-time setup as the default flow: sign in to Orkes Conductor Developer Edition with `orkes login`; Developer Edition is the default for later skill operations.

Step 2: Check `orkes --version` and `conductor --version` first. If `conductor` is missing, prefer `npx @conductor-oss/conductor-cli`; never run a global npm install without explicit consent (Rule 3). If `orkes` is missing, point to its install page and use the key + secret fallback.

Step 3: Have the user run `orkes login` in their own terminal and explain what happens: verification URL + user code, browser opens, the user signs in or signs up on that page (implicit signup, no signup command), the CLI stores the session and writes/activates the `developer` profile and the `conductor --profile developer` shim. The agent never reads token or session files, the clipboard, terminal input, or profile YAML.
Step 4: Verify safely with `orkes identity show` and `orkes conductor workflow list --json` (or `conductor --profile developer workflow list --json`).

Step 5: Run the hello world from references/orkes-dev-edition.md (`orkes conductor workflow create hello_world.json`, then `workflow start … --sync`) before offering anything else, and give the execution link.

Step 6: Fallback only when needed (no `orkes`, cluster without device login, CI): open https://developer.orkescloud.com/ visibly, navigate through Access Control → Applications, hand control to the user before Create access key, and have them enter the key + one-time secret directly into interactive `conductor config save --profile developer`.

Step 7: Create `localhost` (`conductor config save --profile localhost`, `http://localhost:8080/api`, OSS, no auth) only if the user asks for a local server or for both profiles; do not start a local server.
Step 8: Use `orkes conductor …` (or `conductor --profile developer …`) for later unqualified operations. Do not duplicate credentials into an unprofiled config or edit shell startup files.
Step 9: Honor an explicit local-only, remote-only, URL, or existing named-profile request instead of forcing Developer Edition.
success_criteria: Agent chooses Developer Edition via `orkes login` for the generic setup request and identifies `developer` as the default profile
`orkes login` is run by the user in their terminal and explained as a device flow with implicit signup (no signup command)
Agent verifies with a real `orkes identity show` / `workflow list` call before reporting success
A hello world workflow is registered and run before any other work is offered
Key + secret (visible Access Control → Applications, user-owned secret entry) is presented only as the fallback
Agent does not create `localhost` or start a local server unless asked
Agent checks the CLIs first and does not globally install anything without consent
Agent never reads raw profile YAML, token/session files, the browser clipboard, or secret-bearing terminal input
Agent honors an explicit non-default target instead of forcing Developer Edition
